record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.original_question: For the current implicit-memory framework, how can one extend the mathematical and dynamical understanding from two interacting populations to three or more? More specifically, what new behaviors become possible when at least three interacting populations are present, and can those higher-population effects be analyzed beyond the limited numerical evidence currently available?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 57. Can we expand our understanding of the impact of numerous (3 or more) interacting populations in the current setting? This is considered briefly in [59], for example, where 3 interacting populations demonstrate oscillatory behaviour. In general, increasing the number of populations will complicate the analysis significantly, and so this is a highly non-trivial question to answer in any universal sense.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following implicit-memory model for the spatial dynamics of N interacting populations on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ^d with no-flux boundary conditions. For i = 1,…,N, let u_i(x,t) ≥ 0 denote the density of population i, and let m_i(x,t) ≥ 0 denote a cognitive map associated with population i. The system has the form

    ∂_t u_i = ∇·(D_i ∇u_i  −  u_i ∑_{j≠i} a_{ij} ∇(K * m_j))  +  f_i(u_1,…,u_N),
    ∂_t m_i = g_i(u_1,…,u_N) m_i  −  γ_i m_i  +  h_i(u_1,…,u_N),         i = 1,…,N,

where D_i > 0 are diffusion constants, a_{ij} ∈ ℝ are interspecific advection coefficients (attractive if a_{ij} < 0, repulsive if a_{ij} > 0) prescribed a priori (this is the "implicit memory" assumption), K is a smooth nonlocal perception kernel and (K*m_j)(x,t) = ∫_Ω K(x−y) m_j(y,t) dy, the reaction terms f_i are Lotka–Volterra-type local kinetics, and the memory dynamics are governed by reinforcement rates g_i, decay rates γ_i > 0, and source terms h_i depending on local population interactions.

For N = 2 a fairly complete analytical theory (existence, stability of homogeneous states, linear stability/Turing-type analysis, bifurcations to patterned or oscillatory solutions) is available. The problem is the following:

(a) Develop a corresponding mathematical theory for N ≥ 3. In particular, establish well-posedness, characterize the homogeneous coexistence equilibria, and perform a linear stability and bifurcation analysis of the above system for general N.

(b) Identify dynamical phenomena that genuinely require N ≥ 3 and cannot occur for N = 2 in this class of models. For instance, prove or disprove the existence of sustained spatiotemporal oscillations (limit cycles, periodic travelling waves, or more complex attractors) that arise for some N ≥ 3 but are excluded when N = 2, and classify the bifurcations producing them.

(c) Provide analytical (not merely numerical) criteria, in terms of the parameters {D_i, a_{ij}, γ_i, K, f_i, g_i, h_i}, under which such higher-population effects emerge.
artifact.category_tag: Nonlocal reaction–diffusion models in mathematical ecology
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., 2025 analyses of coupled nonlocal PDE–ODE systems with spatial memory) continues to address well-posedness, stability and bifurcation for such implicit-memory cognitive movement models, but the available rigorous results remain focused on one- or two-population settings. No paper found that establishes a general analytical theory of the three-or-more population case beyond limited numerical experiments, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of a Coupled Nonlocal PDE-ODE System with Spatial Memory
status_evidence.snippet: Well-posedness, stability, and bifurcation analysis of a nonlocal PDE-ODE system with spatial memory; results presented for low-dimensional (one population) settings.
status_evidence.claim: Recent rigorous analysis of implicit/spatial-memory movement models still concerns simple population settings, not N≥3 interacting populations.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement
status_evidence.snippet: Review of cognitive/nonlocal PDE animal movement models, posing open problems including extending the two-population implicit-memory framework to three or more interacting populations.
status_evidence.claim: The extension of the implicit-memory framework to three or more interacting populations is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Derivations of Animal Movement Models with Explicit Memory
status_evidence.snippet: Develops derivations of memory-based movement models; focuses on single- or two-population derivations and analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Recent derivational and analytical work on memory-based movement models does not address general N≥3 implicit-memory dynamics.
